text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Brentford and Everton.
Brentford’s seven-game unbeaten run in the league game ended against Newcastle in their previous outing.
Callum Wilson’s 64th-minute penalty proved to be the only goal of the match, with manager Thomas Frank also losing left-back Rico Henry to a suspected long-term injury.
The Bees drew three of their first four matches, with their only win of the new campaign coming against Fulham at Craven Cottage.
Brentford are currently in 11th position in the table and have just one clean sheet to their name this season.
Everton survived on the final day of the Premier League season last term and have had a miserable start to the new campaign.
The Toffees have lost four of their opening five games, with their only point coming against newly promoted Sheffield United.
Additionally, their draw with the Blades was the only time that they have scored in the league, conceding a combined seven goals without reply against Fulham, Aston Villa, Wolves and Arsenal.
They are without a victory in their last four away trips to Brentford in all competitions (drawing two and losing two), since a 4-2 win in the second tier in September 1952.
Brentford make two changes to the side that lost to Newcastle in the previous match.
Henry is set to miss the rest of the season and is replaced by Roerslev at left-back.
Mee also misses out through injury.
As a result, Frank has decided to add another attacker into the mix, with Schade coming in.
Everton make one alteration to the team that lost to Arsenal last time out.
Garner comes into the side and takes the place of Danjuma, who drops to the bench.
Schade went down injured in the warm-up and will not be able to play.
Lewis-Potter will take his place in the attack.
Both teams are now on the pitch and the game will start soon.
Everton get this Premier League clash under way.
Beto makes the most of a poor throw-in and drives towards the box.
However, he is slow on the ball and is tackled by Janelt.
Young is shown an early yellow card after fouling Lewis-Potter on the edge of the box.
Mbeumo and Jensen are over the free-kick.
The latter takes and curls his attempt well wide of the post.
Garner whips a cross into the middle of the box, but it goes over the head of Beto and Collins gets it away.
Branthwaite chips the ball forward to Beto, who flicks a pass onto Doucoure.
He runs into the box and looks to work space for a shot, but Pinnock forces him back.
GOALLL! DOUCOURE SCORES! 1-0 EVERTON! What a start for the away side.
Garner floats a cross into the middle of the box after a corner from the right was cleared away.
Captain Tarkowski knocks a header into the path of Doucoure, who blasts his effort past Flekken.
Tarkowski decides to be unselfish in the box.
He could direct his header towards the goal but has the intelligence to put the ball into the path of Doucoure, who does the rest with an emphatic finish.
Brentford have conceded 4 first-half goals in six games, only Burnley (six) and Nottingham Forest (six) have conceded more in the Premier League this season.
Young bursts down the right and looks for Beto with a cross.
However, his attempt is poor and floats out for a goal-kick.
Onana finds Beto inside Brentford's half after the hosts give away possession cheaply.
He looks to turn past a couple of defenders and move into space, but he is crowded out.
Brentford have been unusually poor with a couple of their passes in the early stages of the game.
They have been too short, allowing the Everton players to get in and make quick interceptions.
Mykolenko is caught in possession by Mbeumo, who plays a pass inside to Wissa before breaking away.
The striker then looks to complete a one-two but plays the ball straight off the pitch.
WIDE! McNeil goes close! Beto has won a couple of battles in the air and does well again to knock the ball into the path of McNeil.
The winger drives down the left side of the box before dragging a shot across the goal and just wide.
Mykolenko wins the ball inside Brentford's defensive third and slides a pass into Doucoure.
He then looks for Beto with a cross, but the Bees get it away.
McNeil goes short with a free-kick, allowing Garner to chip a cross into the box.
Onana gets on the end of it and heads it towards the goal, but his effort goes just wide of the target.
Pinnock has been active in the opening 18 minutes of the game.
He has had to constantly be ready for Everton to look for Beto with long passes forward and has already made a couple of crucial interceptions with his head.
Collins is standing on the ball inside Brentford's half and is being urged by the crowd to do something with it.
Everton are staying off the defender and are letting him make a decision.
SAVE! McNeil has put a couple of high crosses into Beto but goes low this time.
Pinnock sticks a foot out to make an interception.
However, he plays the ball straight into the feet of Mykolenko, who shoots straight at Flekken from close range.
Everton burst forward on the counter, with McNeil rushing down the left before supplying a low cross into the heart of the box.
Doucoure and Garner make darting runs, but it goes between them both and away from danger.
Pinnock looks to switch the play from left to right towards Mbeumo, but it goes over the head of the winger.
He thrashes his arms in frustration before clapping his hands together in encouragement.
BAR! Everton should have scored again through Doucoure.
Tarkowski launches a pass out of the defence and towards the midfielder, who uses his strength to push away Roerslev inside the box.
He takes it down well before crashing the bar.
GOALLL! JENSEN SCORES! 1-1! Brentford have struggled to create any meaningful attacks in this game but have netted the equaliser.
Wissa battles for the ball in the air, with it dropping to Janelt on the edge of the box.
He shapes to shoot before playing a pass across to Jensen, who drills his shot off the post and into the net.

events.action: drills his shot off the post and into the net

text: Pickford gets a touch on it but it is not enough.
There is a VAR check for offside, but the goal stands.
The assist from Janelt is excellent, he looks to shoot but is aware of Jensen to his right and finds him with a perfect pass.
Jensen still has a lot to do and finishes the chance well.
There was just 89 seconds between Doucoure hitting the woodwork for Everton and Jensen scoring Brentford's equaliser.
Everton were the better side until Brentford scored and had a couple of clear chances to score a second goal.
Now it is Brentford who have the momentum.
Collins looks to slide a pass down the middle of the pitch to Wissa, but Branthwaite stays tight to the striker and pokes the ball away.
Young launches the ball forward towards Beto, who uses his strength to get away from Collins.
However, he has to wait for support and plays the ball back into the midfield.
WIDE! Beto misses the target this time.
Gueye uses his body to trick Norgaard, shaping to go left and instead moving to the right.
He has space ahead of him and slips a throughball into the path of Beto, who scoops his shot wide of the post.
Jensen launches a long thrown-in into the box.
Beto clears it as far as Janelt, who has his shot blocked.
Hickey collects the rebound but blasts his strike over the target.
Collins plays a poor pass in Everton's half, allowing the away side to break away on the counter.
Beto rushes away and moves down the left side of the box before dragging a cross into a dangerous area.
However, it is behind Onana, who goes down under little contact.
CHANCE! Gueye gives away possession inside Everton's half, with Wissa collecting the loose ball before sliding a pass across to Mbeumo.
He then flashes it across the box, with Tarkowski sliding across the line.
He cannot turn it behind but might have distracted Lewis-Potter, who could not poke it in.
Garner flicks a pass inside to Gueye on the edge of the box.
He has Beto and Doucoure as options in the middle but misses the target with a poor shot.
Gueye drives forward and is not put under pressure before slotting a pass down the right of the box to Beto.
He flashes a cross-shot into a promising position, but nobody is there to get on the end of it.
The former Udinese attacker then looks around and questions the support from his team-mates.
There will be three minutes of additional time.
Gueye gives the ball away cheaply inside Everton's half, allowing Brentford to come forward.
A ball from the left is played into the box towards Wissa, who looks to turn past Branthwaite but goes down.
He wants a penalty, but the referee ignores his claims.
HALF-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-1 EVERTON
Brentford scored with their only shot on target of the half to cancel out Doucoure's opener and send the teams into the break level.
Everton dominated the early exchanges of the fixture and could have scored two or three if they were clinical.
Doucoure broke the deadlock, thrashing Tarkowski's knockdown into the net.
McNeil then dragged a shot wide, with Flekken also denying Mykolenko from close range.
Doucoure then rattled the bar, with the Bees netting an equaliser 89 seconds later.
Jensen drilled his shot off the post and into the bottom corner from the right side of the box.

events.action: drilled his shot off the post and into the bottom corner

text: Pickford got a glove on it but couldn't keep it out.
Beto then had the chance to open his account in the Premier League but scooped his strike wide.
Everton will go into the dressing room disappointed that they do not have complete control of the game.
They created plenty of chances at the start of the match and made the most of Brentford's unusual sloppiness in possession, but couldn't score more than one.
McNeil has been excellent on the counter and Beto has constantly been a threat.
As for the home side, they recovered well to end the half strongly.
Frank's men are starting to put the Toffees under pressure and are targeting Gueye, who has made a couple of poor passes.
Brentford get the ball rolling again.
No changes at the break.

Brentford lost their last Premier League game when going into half-time level against Newcastle, not since January 2022 have the Bees lost successive such games, doing so against Manchester United and Wolves.
Jensen goes down after a heavy collision with Gueye.
The elbow of the Everton man accidentally hit the back of his head, with the medical staff on the pitch.
Jensen will be able to continue and is now back on the pitch.
Gueye looks for Doucoure with a cross into the box, but his attempt is wayward.
Doucoure sticks his thumb in the air to show appreciation for the effort.
Beto wins possession on the halfway line and looks up before attempting an ambitious effort from range.
The striker looks to chip Flekken but gets no height on his strike.
McNeil works the ball onto his left foot and curls a low effort towards the goal from the edge of the box.
However, his effort goes straight at Flekken.
McNeil stayed on the left flank for the majority of the first half but is roaming inside at the start of the second.
He is picking up positions in the middle of the pitch and is not being tracked by the Brentford players when he is in that position.
McNeil's pass into Doucoure is intercepted and Brentford come away with the ball.
Mbeumo has a crowd of Everton players ahead of him and skips past Gueye before losing control of possession.
The hands of Branthwaite hit his face and he wants a free-kick.
However, the referee lets the game continue.
Everton win a free-kick on the left.
McNeil finds Tarkowski, who heads the ball across the box towards Onana.
He gets above his marker and gets an effort away, but it goes wide of the post from a tight angle.
Everton are patient with possession outside the box and are committing men forward.
Tarkowski then lofts a cross into the box to Beto, who angles a header wide of the post.
Flekken watched it all the way and looked confident that it was going off target.
Brentford are making two changes to try and alter the outcome of the game.
Roerslev is the first player to come off and he is replaced by Ajer.
Onyeka also makes his way onto the pitch and takes the place of Janelt, who got the assist for Brentford's goal.
Calvert-Lewin is still waiting to come on for Everton.
Beto has impressed for Everton and has shown his ability to challenge for the ball in the air and get into promising attacking positions.
Calvert-Lewin comes on and will play up front.
Mbeumo looks to rush past Onana on the left, but the Belgium international gets his foot across to win possession.
McNeil then collects it and whips a cross into the box that is headed away by Pinnock.
GOALLLLL! TARKOWSKI SCORES! 2-1 EVERTON! The away side have been the better side since the restart and it is Tarkowski with the goal.
McNeil's corner from the right is inviting, with the centre-back rushing free from his marker and powering his header into the net.

events.action: powering his header into the net

text: McNeil is forced to wait to take the corner before putting in a perfect cross.
His ball into the box matches the run of Tarkowski, who plants an emphatic header into the net.

events.action: plants an emphatic header into the net

text: Mykolenko rushes down the left and sends a low cross into the box.
Flekken looks like he has it under control but Hickey takes no risks and heads it behind.
GOALLLLL! CALVERT-LEWIN WITH A CLINICAL FINISH! 3-1 EVERTON! Collins loses the ball inside his own half, allowing Garner to come away with possession.
He has Doucoure to his left but threads an excellent pass to Calvert-Lewin in the middle, who finishes the chance with composure.
Garner plays a key part in the goal.
His tackle on Collins is excellent, with the midfielder coming away with the ball.
He has space ahead of him and could have made a pass to early, but waits for Calvert-Lewin to move into space before finding the striker.
He is one-on-one with Flekken and makes no mistake.
Calvert-Lewin has scored his first Premier League goal away from home in open play since May 2021 against West Ham, he three goals away from home since in the league were all penalties before today.
Ghoddos is introduced for the final 17 minutes and is replaced by Ghoddos.
Everton are in complete control at the moment.
Brentford are giving the ball away cheaply and are committing a lot of fouls.
Mbeumo is shown a yellow card for a foul on McNeil.
Onana makes his way off after an all-action performance in the midfield.
Danjuma takes his place.
Collins shows a spurt of energy and brings the ball out of the defence before curling a pass out to Ghoddos.
He waits for support and finds Mbeumo with a cross, but his attempt from the right side of the box is saved by Pickford.
Everton are making Brentford do all the work off the ball.
They are playing a lot of neat passes around their half, forcing the Bees to close them down.
Ghoddos is shown a yellow card for pulling back Young, who was breaking into Brentford's half.
The hosts are showing a lot of signs of frustration as they have not been able to get going since the restart.
Onyeka tries to float a hopeful ball over the top of Everton's defence towards Mbeumo, but it goes nowhere near the attacker.
Pickford claims it, with Wissa putting him under immediate pressure.
Danjuma displays some nice footwork to get past a defender before rolling a pass into Doucoure, who immediately finds Calvert-Lewin.
The striker looks to spin in possession but runs into Collins.
Lewis-Potter has possession on the left and cuts the ball onto his right foot before curling a cross into the box.
However, it is too high and too close to Pickford, who makes an easy catch.
Everton have won none of their last 13 away Premier League visits to London (drawing five and losing eight) since a 1-0 win at West Ham United in May 2021.
Dyche’s last London win was also in May 2021, 2-0 vs Fulham with Burnley, with Dyche winless in seven since then (drawing five and losing two).
Tarkowski looks to score his second of the game after getting onto the end of Garner's corner but knocks his attempt well over the bar.
Olakigbe makes his way onto the pitch for Brentford to make a brief appearance.
Lewis-Potter is now off.
The Everton fans are cheering every pass that they make, with the away side playing it around with confidence.
There will be six minutes of additional time.
Branthwaite is shown a yellow card for a tackle on Onyeka, who dribbled past him before being fouled.
Norgaard finds Mbeumo on the right, who cuts inside before swinging a cross into the box.
Branthwaite is in the middle and clears it away with his boot.
Ghoddos curls a pass with the outside of his foot into the path of Olakigbe, who rushes towards the byline and into the box.
Danjuma tracks his run and makes contact with his shirt before releasing it.
Olakigbe goes down but nothing is given.
The 19-year-old has shown a couple of bright moments in this game since being introduced.
FULL-TIME: BRENTFORD 1-3 EVERTON
Tarkowski bagged a goal and an assist to help Everton to their first win of the season away to Brentford.
Dyche's men started the game strongly and scored the opener through Doucoure.
He made the most of Tarkowski's headed pass and blasted the ball into the net.

events.action: headed pass and blasted the ball into the net

text: The Toffees were in control of the match and should have scored again.
McNeil struck an effort wide, with Mykolenko shooting straight at Flekken.
Doucoure then rattled the bar before Frank's side found an equaliser.
Jansen got on the end of Janelt's disguised pass and powered his low effort in off the post.
Beto then had a scoring chance but made a mess of the finish and shot well wide.
The Bees were sloppy after the break and Everton were able to punish them.
Tarkowski scored against his old side, running away from his marker to power McNeil's corner past Flekken.
The Toffees then netted their third four minutes later.
Garner won the ball off Collins and found Calvert-Lewin, who finished the chance with composure.
Brentford have won just once this season and have lost their last two fixtures in the Premier League.
The Bees will host Arsenal in the third round of the EFL Cup before heading to Nottingham Forest in the league.
As for Everton, they travel to Villa in the cup, where they lost 4-0 earlier in the campaign.
The Toffees then welcome Luton Town in the league.
That's all for today, goodbye.
